No obfuscation, suspicious behavior, or supply-chain red flags are present.

The package conflicts with alternative versions (`sunsetr-git`, `sunsetr-git-debug`) and replaces one, which is normal for binary packages to avoid co-installation issues. All declared dependencies and metadata are appropriate for the described software.

The SHA-256 checksum is explicitly provided and matches the expected value for the release asset, ensuring integrity. The package installs the binary to `/usr/bin`, the license to `/usr/share/licenses`, a systemd user service file to `/usr/lib/systemd/user`, and documentation to `/usr/share/doc`. While the checksum is specified and valid, the source is a pre-built binary, meaning the build is not reproducible and users must trust the binary provided by the upstream maintainer. The PKGBUILD itself follows AUR packaging best practices and shows no evidence of supply-chain compromise.
